```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Bienert et al. (2010) sedated ICU patients with a constant propofol infusion
for several days and asked whether the light-dark cycle changes propofol
pharmacokinetics, its effect on the Bispectral Index (BIS), or the routinely
monitored vital signs. The paper contributes three independently fitted
models, each packaged as its own file:

| Model file | What it describes |
|---|---|
| `Bienert_2010_propofol` | Two-compartment propofol PK with systolic blood pressure on clearance, and a direct-effect Emax model for BIS |
| `Bienert_2010_heartRate` | 24-hour cosine rhythm in heart rate |
| `Bienert_2010_bodyTemperature` | 24-hour cosine rhythm in body temperature |

No circadian term was retained for propofol clearance or EC50 (objective
function drops of 4.9 and 13.5, below the 13.8 threshold for two degrees of
freedom at P < 0.001), nor for systolic or diastolic blood pressure or blood
oxygen saturation.

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Bienert_2010_propofol"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-010-9161-5> (open access,
  [PMC2889282](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC2889282/))

No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (checked
2026-11-19).

# Population

Eleven adult ICU patients (8 male, 3 female; age 63 +/- 11 years, 53-85;
weight 72.6 +/- 22.8 kg, 50-95) were sedated with propofol for more than 24 h
(Table 1). Patient 3 had no blood samples and was excluded, so ten patients
contributed data to every model. Patients with neuromuscular blockade, head
trauma or neurological disorders that could alter the EEG were excluded, and
no vasopressors were given. After a 1.5 mg/kg initial dose the maintenance
infusion was constant at 0.7-0.9 mg/kg/h (one patient needed rate changes).
Arterial plasma propofol, BIS, blood pressure, heart rate, oxygen saturation
and body temperature were recorded every hour during the second and third
day of infusion, and propofol was also sampled 3-240 min after the infusion
stopped. The mean steady-state propofol concentration was 0.48 +/- 0.21 mg/L.

The same information is available programmatically, for example
`readModelDb("Bienert_2010_propofol")()$population`.

# Propofol PK and BIS

## Virtual cohort

Each virtual patient receives the 1.5 mg/kg initial dose and a constant
infusion drawn uniformly from 0.7-0.9 mg/kg/h for 72 h, followed by the
paper's post-infusion sampling times. Weight and systolic blood pressure are
drawn from the Table 1 means and SDs, clipped to the observed ranges.
Systolic blood pressure is held constant within a patient (see Assumptions).

```{r pk-cohort}
set.seed(2010)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2010)

n_pk <- 200
t_inf <- 72 * 60 # infusion length (min)
post <- c(3, 5, 10, 15, 30, 60, 120, 180, 240)

pk_subj <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_pk),
  WT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pk, 72.6, 22.8), 50), 95),
  SBP = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_pk, 135, 19.4), 85), 191),
  rate_mgkgh = runif(n_pk, 0.7, 0.9)
)

pk_dose <- bind_rows(
  pk_subj |> mutate(time = 0, amt = 1.5 * WT, rate = 0, evid = 1),
  pk_subj |>
    mutate(
      time = 0, rate = rate_mgkgh * WT / 60,
      amt = rate * t_inf, evid = 1
    )
)
pk_obs <- tidyr::crossing(
  pk_subj,
  time = c(seq(0, t_inf, by = 60), t_inf + post)
) |>
  mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0)

pk_events <- bind_rows(pk_dose, pk_obs) |>
  # Two declared endpoints (Cc, BIS): observation rows name the ODE state
  # and carry dvid = 1 so rxode2 returns every endpoint column.
  mutate(
    cmt = "central", dvid = ifelse(evid == 0, 1L, NA_integer_),
    treatment = "0.7-0.9 mg/kg/h"
  ) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  select(id, time, amt, rate, evid, cmt, dvid, WT, SBP, treatment)
```

## Simulation

```{r pk-sim}
mod_pk <- readModelDb("Bienert_2010_propofol")
sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = pk_events, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
# Typical patient: 72.6 kg, 0.8 mg/kg/h, SBP at the 135 mmHg centring value.
typ_rate <- 0.8 * 72.6 / 60
typ_events <- bind_rows(
  tibble(time = 0, amt = 1.5 * 72.6, rate = 0, evid = 1),
  tibble(time = 0, amt = typ_rate * t_inf, rate = typ_rate, evid = 1),
  tibble(time = c(seq(0, t_inf, by = 60), t_inf + post), amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0)
) |>
  mutate(
    id = 1, cmt = "central", SBP = 135,
    dvid = ifelse(evid == 0, 1L, NA_integer_)
  ) |>
  arrange(time, desc(evid))
sim_pk_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pk), events = typ_events) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

## Concentration and BIS over time

```{r figure-1-2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
# Compare with Figures 1 and 2 of Bienert 2010: hourly concentrations and
# BIS through the second and third day of infusion and after it stops.
pk_long <- sim_pk |>
  filter(time >= 24 * 60) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, BIS) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, BIS), names_to = "output") |>
  group_by(output, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(value, 0.05), Q50 = median(value), Q95 = quantile(value, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
typ_long <- sim_pk_typ |>
  filter(time >= 24 * 60) |>
  select(time, Cc, BIS) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, BIS), names_to = "output")

ggplot(pk_long, aes(time / 60)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = Q50)) +
  geom_line(data = typ_long, aes(y = value), linetype = "dashed", colour = "blue") +
  facet_wrap(~output, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time since start of infusion (h)", y = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Median and 90% interval of 200 virtual patients; dashed: typical\n",
      "patient (72.6 kg, 0.8 mg/kg/h, SBP 135 mmHg). Compare Figures 1-2."
    )
  )
```

## PKNCA: average concentration over the study period

The paper reports the mean steady-state concentration during the second and
third day of infusion, 0.48 +/- 0.21 mg/L. PKNCA's `cav` over 24-72 h is the
simulated counterpart.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
sim_nca <- bind_rows(
  sim_nca,
  sim_nca |> distinct(id, treatment) |> mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
) |>
  distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, treatment, time)

dose_df <- pk_events |>
  filter(evid == 1, rate > 0) |>
  mutate(dur = t_inf) |>
  select(id, time, amt, dur, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(
  dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id,
  route = "intravascular", duration = "dur"
)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 24 * 60, end = 72 * 60,
  cav = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

cav <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cav") |>
  pull(PPORRES)

tibble(
  `NCA parameter` = "Cav, 24-72 h (mg/L)",
  Simulated = sprintf("%.2f +/- %.2f", mean(cav), sd(cav)),
  Published = "0.48 +/- 0.21",
  `Difference of means (%)` = round(100 * (mean(cav) - 0.48) / 0.48, 1)
) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Simulated vs published steady-state propofol concentration (mean +/- SD).")
```

The simulated mean sits about 15-20% below the published 0.48 mg/L. With a
typical clearance of 2.65 L/min and a typical 72.6 kg patient at 0.8 mg/kg/h
(0.97 mg/min), the typical steady state is 0.97 / 2.65 = 0.37 mg/L, and the
48.6% IIV on clearance lifts the cohort mean to about 0.41 mg/L. The
observed mean also includes the extra boluses individual patients received
and one patient's rate changes, neither of which the paper tabulates, so a
small shortfall is expected; the model is not adjusted for it.

```{r pk-checks}
# Structural: a mis-transcribed clearance or a unit slip (L/min vs L/h)
# moves the mean by 50% or a factor of 60.
stopifnot(abs(mean(cav) - 0.48) / 0.48 < 0.30)

# Deterministic typical-patient steady state, infusion rate / CL, and the
# corresponding BIS from Eq. 2.
css_typ <- sim_pk_typ$Cc[sim_pk_typ$time == t_inf]
stopifnot(abs(css_typ - (0.8 * 72.6 / 60) / 2.65) / css_typ < 0.01)
bis_typ <- sim_pk_typ$BIS[sim_pk_typ$time == t_inf]
stopifnot(abs(bis_typ - (100 - 100 * css_typ / (1.98 + css_typ))) < 1e-6)
```

The typical patient settles at `r round(css_typ, 3)` mg/L with BIS
`r round(bis_typ, 1)`, within the 80-95 band in which most of the observed
BIS values of Figure 2 lie.

## Systolic blood pressure on clearance

```{r sbp-effect}
tibble(SBP = c(85, 110, 135, 160, 191)) |>
  mutate(
    `CL (L/min)` = round(2.65 * (1 - 0.00714 * (SBP - 135)), 2),
    `Typical Css at 0.97 mg/min (mg/L)` = round(0.968 / `CL (L/min)`, 2)
  ) |>
  rename(`SBP (mmHg)` = SBP) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical clearance across the observed SBP range (Table 1: 85-191 mmHg).")
```

# Circadian rhythms in heart rate and body temperature

Both rhythm models are evaluated at the clock time of each record, which the
models take as the covariate `TCLOCK`. In Eq. 7 the cosine argument is
`t - acrophase + T`, with `t` the time since the start of infusion and `T` the
clock time at the start; `t + T` is therefore the record's clock time. The
virtual patients start their infusion at 15:00 and are followed hourly over
the second and third day, as in the study.

```{r rhythm-cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2011)
n_vs <- 200
start_clock <- 15
vs_events <- tidyr::crossing(id = seq_len(n_vs), time = seq(24, 72, by = 1)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, TCLOCK = (start_clock + time) %% 24)

mod_hr <- readModelDb("Bienert_2010_heartRate")
mod_temp <- readModelDb("Bienert_2010_bodyTemperature")

sim_hr <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_hr, events = vs_events) |> as.data.frame()
sim_temp <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_temp, events = vs_events) |> as.data.frame()

typ_vs_events <- vs_events |> filter(id == 1)
typ_hr <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_hr), events = typ_vs_events) |> as.data.frame()
typ_temp <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_temp), events = typ_vs_events) |> as.data.frame()
```

```{r figure-3-4, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 6}
# Compare with Figures 3 and 4: the population-predicted (typical) rhythm
# over the second and third day, with the dark period 20:00-08:00 shaded.
dark <- tibble(clock_start = c(20, 44, 68)) |>
  mutate(
    xmin = pmax(clock_start - start_clock, 24),
    xmax = pmin(clock_start - start_clock + 12, 72)
  ) |>
  filter(xmax > xmin)

rhythm <- bind_rows(
  sim_hr |>
    group_by(time) |>
    summarise(Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95)) |>
    left_join(typ_hr |> select(time, typical = hr), by = "time") |>
    mutate(output = "Heart rate (beats/min)"),
  sim_temp |>
    group_by(time) |>
    summarise(Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05), Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95)) |>
    left_join(typ_temp |> select(time, typical = body_temperature), by = "time") |>
    mutate(output = "Body temperature (degC)")
)

ggplot(rhythm, aes(time)) +
  geom_rect(
    data = dark, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey85"
  ) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = typical), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~output, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time since start of infusion (h)", y = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "Dashed: typical rhythm; band: 90% interval of simulated observations.\n",
      "Infusion started at 15:00. Compare Figures 3-4."
    )
  )
```

## Checks against the paper

The paper states the peak times, the relative amplitudes and, in the
Discussion, the absolute temperature amplitude (0.12 degC). These are
properties of the typical rhythm and are checked exactly.

```{r rhythm-checks}
peak_clock <- function(d, col) {
  fine <- tibble(TCLOCK = seq(0, 23.99, by = 0.01))
  ev <- fine |> mutate(id = 1, time = seq_len(n()), evid = 0, amt = 0)
  out <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(d), events = ev) |> as.data.frame()
  list(peak = fine$TCLOCK[which.max(out[[col]])], max = max(out[[col]]), min = min(out[[col]]))
}
p_hr <- peak_clock(mod_hr, "hr")
p_temp <- peak_clock(mod_temp, "body_temperature")

checks <- tibble(
  Quantity = c(
    "HR peak clock time (h)", "HR amplitude (% of mesor)",
    "Temperature peak clock time (h)", "Temperature amplitude (degC)"
  ),
  Model = c(
    p_hr$peak, 100 * (p_hr$max - p_hr$min) / 2 / 90.5,
    p_temp$peak, (p_temp$max - p_temp$min) / 2
  ),
  Paper = c(14, 4.8, 21.4, 0.12)
)
knitr::kable(checks, digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  abs(p_hr$peak - 14) < 0.02, abs(p_temp$peak - 21.4) < 0.02,
  abs(checks$Model[2] - 4.8) < 0.01, abs(checks$Model[4] - 0.12) < 0.005
)
```

Table 1 gives the spread of all recorded heart rates and temperatures
(SD 15.7 beats/min and 0.5 degC). The models reproduce that spread from the
IIV on the mesor, the rhythm and the residual error together, which
independently supports reading the Table 4 percentages as coefficients of
variation (see Assumptions).

```{r rhythm-spread}
spread <- tibble(
  Variable = c("Heart rate (beats/min)", "Body temperature (degC)"),
  `Simulated SD` = c(sd(sim_hr$sim), sd(sim_temp$sim)),
  `Table 1 SD` = c(15.7, 0.5)
) |>
  mutate(Ratio = `Simulated SD` / `Table 1 SD`)
knitr::kable(spread, digits = 2)
# A variance read as a CV (or the residual read as 0.0966%) moves these
# ratios by a factor of two or more.
stopifnot(all(spread$Ratio > 0.7 & spread$Ratio < 1.4))
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV scale.** Tables 2-4 print the IIV rows as 'omega^2 (%)' and the
  Results quote them as percentages ('IIV of clearance equaled 48.6%').
  They are read as coefficients of variation with CV = sqrt(omega^2), so
  omega^2 = CV^2. Reading them as variances would give a heart-rate CV of
  38% and a body-temperature SD above 3 degC, irreconcilable with the Table 1
  spreads checked above. The alternative log-normal conversion
  omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) differs by about 10% for clearance and EC50 and
  negligibly for the vital signs.
- **Body-temperature residual error.** Table 4 prints 0.0996 for the basic
  model and 0.966 for the model with rhythm. The with-rhythm value, 0.966%
  (about 0.36 degC), is used: the observations in Figure 4 scatter around the
  individual predictions by several tenths of a degree, and it reproduces the
  Table 1 SD of 0.5 degC. The basic-model entry is probably a misprint of
  0.996.
- **BIS residual-error row label.** Table 3 labels the residual row
  'sigma prop,Cp2' and its column 'Basic PK model'; both are carried over
  from Table 2. Eq. 5 defines it as the proportional BIS error.
- **No Hill coefficient.** The Results call the PD model a sigmoid Emax
  model, but Eq. 2 and Table 3 have no Hill coefficient; the equation is
  followed.
- **PK driving the BIS model.** The paper does not say whether the BIS
  model was fitted to the basic or the covariate PK model's predictions. The
  packaged file drives BIS with the final (covariate) PK model.
- **Time units.** The PK/PD model keeps the paper's units (min, L, L/min,
  mg/L). The rhythm models use hours and clock time.
- **Virtual cohort.** Systolic blood pressure was recorded hourly and
  enters the model as a time-varying covariate; the simulation holds it at a
  per-patient value drawn from the Table 1 distribution. Extra boluses and
  rate changes are not simulated. Weight and SBP are drawn from normal
  distributions with the Table 1 mean and SD, clipped to the observed range.
- **Excluded covariates.** Weight, age, initial triglycerides, heart rate,
  diastolic blood pressure, body temperature and oxygen saturation were
  screened and not retained.
